routes.description: Establish that current research findings remain too remote from a materially adequate account of life's emergence and that broader representations of those findings convey substantially greater explanatory proximity than the evidence supports.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the remaining transition from simple chemistry to organized, heritable, evolving cellular systems is shown to be unresolved under meaningful empirical criteria, while current research claims or narratives are shown to obscure or exceed that limitation.

motionBridge.description: Connect the unresolved chemistry-to-life gap to a substantial mismatch between demonstrated progress and communicated explanatory proximity.

centralBridges.description: Require an account of how simple chemistry becomes materially organized, information-bearing, heritable, and evolvable biological machinery.
Require discriminating empirical standards for metabolism, replication, fidelity, heredity, and life rather than reliance on broadly lifelike behavior.
Show that limited chemical results or early organizing principles do not by themselves warrant claims of substantial proximity to cellular life.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish criticism of present evidentiary adequacy from a claim that a future naturalistic explanation is impossible.
Ground the critique in naturalistic evidentiary requirements rather than a design inference or theological objection.

routes.description: Establish that substantial explanatory progress need not reproduce Earth's exact history or begin with modern cells because experiments and theory can identify testable generative principles linking simple chemistry, information, selection, and evolving organization.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if measurable chemical organization and selection provide a falsifiable staged pathway toward biological functionality, and if present claims are appropriately limited to emerging mechanisms rather than completion of a full historical or cellular account.

motionBridge.description: Connect reproducible, falsifiable steps from chemistry toward evolving organization to a warranted claim that an explanatory pathway is emerging.

centralBridges.description: Identify simple natural principles capable of generating molecular complexity, templating, coupled catalysis, or primitive copying.
Explain how heritable chemical variation and selection can develop increasingly functional organization toward biological systems.
Provide objective measurements and experimental predictions that can distinguish progress from unconstrained historical speculation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate evidence for a general pathway from claims to know the unique molecular sequence followed on early Earth.
Require uncertainty, experimental revision, and collaborative scrutiny to constrain ambitious origin-of-life hypotheses.

sections.title: Scope of Present Claims and the Standard for Overstatement
sections.rationale: This issue determines what current research is claiming, whether an emerging pathway is distinct from a completed explanation, and whether public or scientific extrapolation materially exceeds the demonstrated results.

sections.title: The Explanatory Gap from Simple Chemistry to Cellular Life
sections.rationale: The motion centrally turns on whether the distance between simple chemical environments and organized cellular systems is an unresolved burden-defining gap or a bridgeable sequence whose governing principles are becoming accessible.

sections.title: What Laboratory Chemical Systems Demonstrate
sections.rationale: The relevance of templating, autocatalysis, coupled catalytic organization, and primitive copying determines whether laboratory results disclose mechanisms continuous with life or remain isolated chemical achievements.

sections.title: Operational Definitions and Objective Measures of Life-like Progress
sections.rationale: Standards for information, metabolism, replication, fidelity, complexity, and life establish what observations would count as genuine explanatory progress and keep the dispute empirically testable.

sections.title: Generative Principles, Selection, and Predictive Pathways
sections.rationale: The viability of complexity-based theory, chemical selection, and experimentally testable predictions bears on whether research offers a cumulative natural pathway rather than either a historical narrative or an admission of ignorance.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Current origin-of-life accounts convey substantially more confidence and understanding than the supporting chemical evidence warrants.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Evidence for simple prebiotic chemistry and later cellular life does not explain the unresolved transition between them, and information by itself is not life.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: A future naturalistic explanation remains possible, but current open problems should not be portrayed as though they are already understood.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Information or recursive replication alone cannot explain life's origin without accounting for the material construction and organization of cellular systems.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: The molybdate experiment demonstrates investigator-influenced autocatalysis but does not by itself establish a meaningful pathway toward cellular life.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Primitive information buildup and coupled catalysis should not be treated as proximity to life when increasing knowledge of cellular organization reveals a still more demanding target.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-001.proposition: Origin-of-life research needs agreed empirical criteria that distinguish genuinely living systems from chemical systems displaying merely lifelike behavior.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-002.proposition: Proposed early chemical phenomena remain far removed from even the simplest known cells and their estimated minimum gene-level organization.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-003.proposition: Claims of metabolism or self-replication require operational thresholds for sustained copying and adequate fidelity, rather than loose resemblance to ordinary chemical reactions.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Origin-of-life inquiry should remain a fair, evidence-grounded scientific debate, while intelligent design lacks a demonstrable scientific basis.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Laboratory work can reveal a gradual pathway by which simple chemistry generates complexity capable of evolution without recreating Earth's exact history.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Meteoritic and early-Earth evidence supports a simpler chemical starting world while leaving the precise sequence of prebiotic molecules unresolved.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Syntactically structured information requiring encoding and decoding can mark the transition from ordinary chemistry toward agency or decision-making systems.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: The molybdate system exhibits molecular templating and a coupled set in which catalysts help generate other catalysts, exceeding ordinary autocatalysis.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: An informational-complexity assay can experimentally distinguish biological organization from random chemistry without reconstructing Earth's unique historical pathway.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Simple generative laws may underlie life-like complexity even when those laws are obscured by the intricacy of modern cellular systems.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Simple molybdate chemistry can produce improbable templated structures and coupled catalytic organization without engineered biological sequence information.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: A permissive environment may enable primitive self-copying chemistry to arise, after which selection can develop increasingly functional molecular organization.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-004.proposition: An objective measure of molecular complexity can support a theory in which chemical evolution generates organized complexity beyond already biological systems.
